title: Integral naturality of the normalized lisse pullback square
statement: Fix D,l,E as in [def-real-tensor-pullback-comparison-data]. Let f:X to Y be any scheme morphism between finite-type schemes, without separatedness or base-field linearity. Given normalized realizations aX,aY [def-real-lisse-realization-data], there exist b:Along f aX aY and n:PullNormalized f aX aY b [def-real-lisse-pullback-normalization]. For every integral constructible arrow g:K to L, the naturality equation F(Q g) composed with n.comparison L equals n.comparison K composed with G(Q g), where Q is raw rationalization, F is raw completed pullback followed by aX.J and G is aY.J followed by ordinary rational derived pullback. Naturality on arbitrary rational morphisms and a raw natural isomorphism are deliberately not asserted here.

proof.text: Check the finite-type noetherian qcqs finite-dimensional hypotheses. Apply the specified ordinary-completed integral pullback comparison eta; it is invertible, natural in integral arrows, and on good models has quotient augmentation and zero shifted coordinate.

Use inverse-image localization coherence to identify the coefficient square. The ordinary balanced square flattens a tensor (b tensor m) to ab tensor m and inserts one in its inverse; it carries the actual integral adjunction unit to the rational unit with scalar one. Derive the square using the ringed-topos composition and geometric two-isomorphism comparisons, retaining their counit equations. Compose aX.integral, scalar extension of eta inverse, this square and the image of aY.integral inverse. All factors are integral-natural, giving the asserted equation.

Finite locally free singles are K-flat. On each free chart the inverse eta and scalar square take the pulled-back basis vector to the same vector with coefficient one. Their ordinary balanced inverse defines b.balance. Local bases prove b.preserves, and the same derived square proves naturality. Take H0 using the identity-normalized single identification to obtain b.comparison and n.heart, with the prescribed ordinary and derived unit/counit equations. This includes empty schemes, rank zero, varying ranks and non-base-linear morphisms.
